counting-house: Office where merchants kept their accounts and business records.
humbug: Nonsense or foolish talk; something not to be believed.
gruel: Thin porridge boiled in water or milk, eaten by poor people.
pigtail: Hair gathered and plaited into a single tail hanging down the back.
waistcoat: Sleeveless garment worn under a coat; a vest.
cravat: Wide neckcloth worn folded at the throat by men.
great-coat: Long, heavy overcoat worn for warmth in cold weather.
comforter: Long knitted scarf worn around the neck for warmth.
wrapper: Loose gown or robe worn indoors, especially in the morning.
nightcap: Soft cap worn on the head in bed.
extinguisher: Cone-shaped cap used to put out a candle flame.
brawn: Jellied meat made from a pig's head, often served cold.
copper: Large metal pot heated over a fire, used for boiling water or laundry.
deuce: Mild oath or exclamation of surprise or annoyance.
hearse: Carriage used to carry a copse to its funeral.
bowels: Inner parts of the body; here, the deepest feelings.
ill-will: Bad feeling or hostility toward someone.
liberality: Generosity in giving money or kindness to others.
benevolence: Kindness and a desire to do good for others.
facetious: Joking or teasing in a way that is not serious.
tremulous: Trembling or shaking slightly, as from fear or weakness.
spectre: A ghost or frightening supernatural figure.
phantom: A ghost or spirit that appears but has no solid body.
apparition: A ghost, or a sudden strange figure appearing unexpectedly.
lamp-lighter: Person whose job was to light the street lamps at dusk.
shillings: Old British coins; twenty shillings made one pound.
surplus: Extra amount left over after everything needed has been used.
pathos: Quality in something that makes people feel pity or sadness.
jovial: Cheerful, friendly, and full of good humour.
melancholy: Deep, quiet sadness that lasts for a long time.
ruddy: Having a healthy reddish colour, especially in the face.
mournful: Expressing sorrow or grief in a sad way.
livid: Very pale, grey, or bluish, as from cold, fear, or anger.
spite: Desire to hurt or annoy someone out of malice.
capacious: Able to hold a great deal; roomy and spacious.
genial: Warm, friendly, and cheerful in manner.
furrows: Deep lines or wrinkles, especially on the forehead.
laden: Heavily loaded or weighed down with something.
undisturbed: Not interrupted, disturbed, or moved from a settled state.
undergone: Experienced or gone through something difficult.
endeavoured: Tried hard or made a serious effort to do something.
dense: Thick, crowded together, or hard to see through, as fog or crowds.
poultry: Domestic birds such as geese, turkeys, and chickens kept for food.
lofty: Very high, or noble and dignified in character.
mistletoe: Plant with white berries, hung at Christmas for kissing under.
trade: Business or occupation, especially one needing skill with the hands.
dressing-gown: Loose robe worn over nightclothes or indoors.
ecstasy: Overwhelming feeling of great joy or delight.
sprinkling: A small scattering of something, such as sugar or spice.
bleak: Bare, cold, and grim, with little comfort or hope.
rejoiced: Felt or showed great joy and happiness.
lantern: Protective case holding a light, carried to see in the dark.
fiddler: Person who plays the violin, often for dancing.
